title: No Slippage Protection on Deposits and Withdrawals
rootCause: _depositInternal() only checks sharesReceived > 0 (line 246) with no minimum shares parameter. _withdrawInternal() calls vault.redeem() (line 283) without checking the returned assets amount. The deposit/withdraw external functions don't accept or propagate slippage parameters, and they don't return values that callers could use for post-hoc verification.
impact: Each deposit/withdrawal is exposed to sandwich attacks. For deposits, an attacker inflates the vault share price before the deposit (getting fewer shares) and deflates after. For withdrawals, the reverse. Since authorized clients cannot implement their own slippage checks (no return values, no access to vault share info), the strategy is the only place this can be enforced.
recommendation: Add minSharesOut parameter to deposit functions and minAssetsOut parameter to withdraw functions. Check return values against these minimums. Propagate through external interfaces.
